SENATE, No. 4712 

STATE OF NEW JERSEY

222nd LEGISLATURE



INTRODUCED OCTOBER 1, 2026












Sponsored by:

Senator SHIRLEY K. TURNER

District 15 (Hunterdon and Mercer)









SYNOPSIS

Imposes 10 percent tax on computer processing for
certain artificial intelligence systems and dedicates revenue to "AI Workforce
Impact Transition Fund." 



CURRENT VERSION OF TEXT 

As introduced.










An Act imposing a tax on AI computer processing, dedicating
revenues to the support of individuals displaced from their jobs due to
artificial intelligence, and supplementing Titles 34 and 54 of the Revised
Statutes.



Be It
Enacted by the Senate and General Assembly of
the State of New Jersey:



1. As used in sections 1 through
3 of P.L. ,
c. (C. )
(pending before the Legislature as this bill):

"AI computer processing" means
the performance of computer processing services for use in AI system services
by a qualified AI business.

"AI computer processor" means a
person, including a contracted processor or controlled processor, performing AI
computer processing.

"AI system development" means the
development, training, and refinement of an AI system, including, but not
limited to, the design and training of an AI system that is, or is intended to
be, commercially available and intended, in whole or in part, for business uses
within the State.

"AI system operation" means the
operation, maintenance, or modification of an AI system that is commercially
available and intended, in whole or in part, for business uses within the State.

"AI system services" means services
related to AI system development or AI system operation.

"Artificial intelligence
system" or "AI system" means any machine-based system that processes inputs
using algorithms, statistical models, or neural networks to generate outputs
such as predictions, recommendations, decisions, or content that materially
influence or replace human judgment in performing a job function. "AI system"
includes machine learning systems, large language models, generative artificial
intelligence tools, robotic process automation systems, and automated
decision-making platforms. "AI system" does not include general-purpose
software, standard database management systems, or basic rule-based automation
that does not incorporate learning or adaptive capabilities.

"Contracted processor" means an
AI computer processor, other than a controlled processor, that performs AI
computer processing for use by a qualified AI business in exchange for the
payment of consideration.

"Controlled processor" means an
AI computer processor owned and operated by a qualified AI business, including
any affiliate or subsidiary thereof, which AI computer processor performs AI
computer processing for use by the qualified AI business.

"Director" means the Director
of the Division of Taxation.

"Division" means the Division
of Taxation in the Department of the Treasury.

"Person" means an individual,
business, or other entity.

"Qualified AI business" means
a person engaged in AI system services.

"Token" is a specific unit of
computer processing calculated independently by each service provider, which unit
is uniquely identifiable to the type of computer processing generated and which
unit may: be identified as query processing, model-processing, input-output
processing, or another technical classification; generate a specific billing
based on computer processing services; and be measured in floating-point
operations per second.



2. a. (1) There is imposed
a tax in the amount of 10 percent of the value generated by AI computer
processing performed: by any AI computer processor that is located in the
State; or for use by a qualified AI business engaged in AI system services. 
The tax imposed pursuant to this section shall be paid by the AI computer
processor that performs the AI computer processing.

(2) For the purposes of
determining the tax imposed pursuant to this section, the value generated by AI
computer processing shall be equal to the market value of the tokens required
to perform the AI computer processing, as calculated using the following
methods:

(a) if the AI computer
processing is performed by a contracted processor, the value generated by AI
computer processing shall equal the number of tokens required to perform the AI
computer processing, multiplied by the billing rate per token charged by the AI
computer processor; or

(b) if the AI computer
processing is performed by a controlled processor, the value generated by AI
computer processing shall be calculated pursuant to a method of calculation
approved by the division for the respective AI computer processor.

(3) Notwithstanding any
provision of this subsection to the contrary, when AI computer processing is
performed by an AI computer processor located outside the State for a qualified
AI business, the amount of tax otherwise imposed pursuant to this section shall
be apportioned on the basis of the percentage of the value generated by AI
computer processing for the qualified AI business that is attributable to AI
system services used for or intended for business uses within the State.

b. (1) The Director of the
Division of Taxation shall collect and administer the tax imposed pursuant to
this section. In carrying out the provisions of this section, the director
shall have all powers and authority granted in P.L.1966, c.30 (C.54:32B-1 et
seq.). The tax shall be reported and paid to the director on a quarterly basis
in a manner prescribed by the director.

(2) As applicable, each
person responsible for calculation and payment of the tax imposed, collected,
or required to be paid, collected, or remitted under this section shall have
the same right in respect to collecting the tax from that person's customer or
in respect to non-payment of the tax by the customer as if the tax were a part
of the purchase price of the AI computer processing and payable at the same
time; provided, however, that the director shall be joined as a party in any
action or proceeding brought to collect the tax.

(3) For the purposes of this
subsection, "person responsible for the calculation and payment of the tax" includes:
a person, including a partnership, or corporation; an officer, director,
stockholder, or employee of a corporation; or a member or employee of a
partnership, who as such officer, director, stockholder, employee, or member is
under the duty to pay, collect, or remit the tax imposed in this section.

c. The tax imposed
pursuant to this section shall be governed by the provisions of the State
Uniform Tax Procedure Law, R.S.54:48-1 et seq.

d. Any amounts collected
pursuant to this section shall be deposited into the fund established pursuant
to section 4 of P.L. ,
c. (C. )
(pending before the Legislature as this bill).



3. a. An AI computer
processor subject to tax pursuant to section 2 of P.L. ,
c. (C. )
(pending before the Legislature as this bill) shall retain records of all AI
computer processing performed by the AI computer processor. The records shall
be retained in such form and manner as the division may require, which records
shall be submitted to the division at such intervals as the division may
require and upon the division's request. The records shall include, but need
not be limited to:

(1) the scope and nature of
AI computer processing performed, including information verifying the AI system
services for which the AI computer processing was used, and the qualified AI
business for which the AI computer processing was performed;

(2) the total volume of AI computer
processing performed by the AI computer processor in its capacity as a
controlled processor and in its capacity as a contracted processor,
respectively;

(3) the total value
generated by AI computer processing, performed by the AI computer processor in
its capacity as a controlled processor and in its capacity as a contracted
processor, respectively, including the method of calculation;

(4) the amount of AI
computer processing performed in this State and the value generated by AI
computer processing for a qualified AI business that is attributable to AI
system services used for or intended for business uses within the State; and

(5) any other information
required by the division.

b. A qualified AI business
shall retain records of all AI computer processing performed by an AI computer
processor for use by the qualified AI business engaged in AI system services. 
The records shall be retained in such form and manner as the division may
require, which records shall be submitted to the division at such intervals as
the division may require and upon the division's request. The records shall
include, but need not be limited to:

(1) the scope and nature of
AI computer processing consumed, including information verifying the AI system
services for which the AI computer processing was used, and the AI computer
processor that performed the AI computer processing;

(2) the total volume of AI
computer processing used by the qualified AI business, including the total
volume performed by a controlled processor and a contracted processor,
respectively;

(3) the total value
generated by AI computer processing used by the qualified AI business,
including, but not limited to, receipts documenting the consideration paid to
any contracted processor for the performance of AI computer processing;

(4) the value generated by
AI computer processing used by the qualified AI business that is attributable
to AI system services used for or intended for business uses within the State;
and

(5) any other information
required by the division.



4. a. As used in this
section:

"AI system development" means
the development, training, and refinement of an AI system, including, but not
limited to, the design and training of an AI system that is, or is intended to
be, commercially available and intended, in whole or in part, for business uses
within the State.

"AI system operation" means the
operation, maintenance, or modification of an AI system that is commercially
available and intended, in whole or in part, for business uses within the
State.

"AI system services" means
services related to AI system development or AI system operation.

"Artificial intelligence
system" or "AI system" means any machine-based system that processes inputs
using algorithms, statistical models, or neural networks to generate outputs
such as predictions, recommendations, decisions, or content that materially
influence or replace human judgment in performing a job function. "AI system"
includes machine learning systems, large language models, generative artificial
intelligence tools, robotic process automation systems, and automated
decision-making platforms. "AI system" does not include general-purpose
software, standard database management systems, or basic rule-based automation
that does not incorporate learning or adaptive capabilities.

"Commission" means the State
Employment and Training Commission established pursuant to section 5 of
P.L.1989, c.293 (C.34:15C-2).

"Commissioner" means the
Commissioner of the Department of Labor and Workforce Development.

"Department" means the
Department of Labor and Workforce Development.

"Displaced worker" means an
individual whose employment is terminated or whose job is expected to become
obsolete within 12 months due to the current or expected operation of an AI
system or the performance of AI system services therefor.

"Fund" means the AI Workforce
Impact Transition Fund established pursuant to subsection b. of this section.

b. A dedicated, non-lapsing
"AI Workforce Impact Transition Fund," to be managed and invested by the State
Treasurer, is hereby established by the Department of Labor and Workforce
Development. The monies in the fund shall be dedicated for the support of
displaced workers transitioning to an alternate career, including, but not
limited to: the selection of an alternate career; and the provision of or
assistance in accessing career training. The department shall publish
information about the support available pursuant to this section, including how
an individual may access that support, on the department's Internet website.

c. The fund shall be
credited with:

(1) all monies received
pursuant to subsection d. of section 2 of P.L. ,
c. (C. )
(pending before the Legislature as this bill);

(2) any return on the
investment of monies deposited in the fund; and

(3) any other funds made
available to the department for the purposes outlined in subsection b. of this
section, including but not limited to, appropriations by the Legislature,
federal grants, and donations from private persons.

d. The commissioner is
authorized to expend monies from the AI Workforce Impact Transition Fund,
subject to appropriation by the Legislature, for the following purposes:

(1) the provision of
training services for the support of displaced workers transitioning to an
alternate career, including, but not limited to, the selection of an alternate
career and the provision of, or assistance in accessing, career training;

(2) the provision of grants
to qualified organizations for the design, planning, and implementation of
training programs and services in support of displaced workers;

(3) the provision of student
support services and dual enrollment programs in public high schools;

(4) reasonable
administrative costs incurred by the department, which shall not exceed 10
percent of the revenues deposited into the fund during any fiscal year, except
for additional start-up administrative expenses approved by the Director of the
Office of Management and Budget during the first year of activity for the
training services; and

(5) reasonable costs as
incurred by the commission, which shall not exceed 0.5 percent of the revenues deposited
into the fund during any fiscal year, as required by the commission to design
criteria and conduct an annual evaluation of the training services provided through
the fund.

e. The State Employment
and Training Commission shall annually evaluate the training services provided
through the AI Workforce Impact Transition Fund and shall provide a report to
the commissioner upon completion.

f. Within six months of
the conclusion of each fiscal year, the commissioner shall submit, to the
Governor and, pursuant to section 2 of P.L.1991, c.164 (C.52:14-19.1), to the Legislature,
a written report that includes, but is not limited to: the total revenues deposited
into the fund from each source; the total amounts expended from the fund for
each authorized purpose; grants provided, including the amount and, if
applicable, the names of recipient organizations; the number of workers
supported pursuant to this section; the total number of workers who have become
reemployed; administrative spending; relevant State Employment and Training
Commission evaluation data; and any other information which the commissioner
determines is pertinent to the evaluation of the training services provided through
the AI Workforce Impact Transition Fund.



5. a. The Division of
Taxation shall adopt, pursuant to the "Administrative Procedure Act," P.L.1968,
c.410 (C.52:14B-1 et seq.), any rules and regulations necessary to implement
sections 1 through 3 of P.L. , c. (C. )
(pending before the Legislature as this bill). The rules and regulations
adopted pursuant to this subsection shall include, but shall not be limited to:

(1) standards for the
calculation of value generated by AI computer processing; and

(2) requirements for
documentation and reporting pursuant to section 3 of
P.L. ,
c. (C. )
(pending before the Legislature as this bill).

b. The Department of Labor
and Workforce Development shall adopt, pursuant to the "Administrative
Procedure Act," P.L.1968, c.410 (C.52:14B-1 et seq.), any rules and regulations
necessary to implement section 4 of P.L. ,
c. (C. )
(pending before the Legislature as this bill). The rules and regulations
adopted pursuant to this subsection shall include, but shall not be limited to:

(1) standards for
determining that an individual is a displaced worker; and

(2) the nature and duration
of support available to displaced workers.



6. This act shall take
effect on the January 1 next following the date of enactment, provided that the
Division of Taxation and Department of Labor and Workforce Development may take
such anticipatory action as necessary.


STATEMENT



This bill imposes on AI
computer processors a tax of 10 percent on the value generated by AI computer
processing. The bill dedicates revenues to the support of displaced workers
transitioning to an alternate career due to artificial intelligence.

Under the bill, an AI computer
processor is required to pay the 10 percent tax on the value generated by AI computer
processing. An "AI computer processor" is an entity, including a contracted
processor or controlled processor, performing AI computer processing. "Contracted
processor" means an AI computer processor, other than a controlled processor,
that performs AI computer processing for use by a qualified AI business in
exchange for the payment of consideration. "Controlled processor" means an AI
computer processor owned and operated by a qualified AI business, including any
affiliate or subsidiary thereof, which AI computer processor performs AI
computer processing for use by the qualified AI business.

The bill defines "AI computer
processing" as the performance of computer processing services for use in AI
system services by a qualified AI business. "Qualified AI business" generally means
a person engaged in AI system services. "AI system services" means AI system
development or AI system operation for an AI system that is, or is intended to
be, commercially available and intended, in whole or in part, for business uses
in this State.

"AI system" is defined to mean
any machine-based system that processes inputs using algorithms, statistical
models, or neural networks to generate outputs such as predictions,
recommendations, decisions, or content that materially influence or replace
human judgment in performing a job function.



Calculation of the Tax

An AI computer processor that
performs AI computer processing is required to pay the tax imposed under the
bill in the amount of 10 percent of the value generated by AI computer
processing performed. The tax is imposed on any AI computer processor that is
located in the State and any AI computer processor that performs AI computer
processing for use by a qualified AI business engaged in AI system services.

For the purposes of
determining the tax imposed under the bill, the value generated by AI computer
processing equals the market value of the tokens required to perform the AI
computer processing. A "token" is a specific unit of computer processing calculated
independently by each service provider, which unit is uniquely identifiable to
the type of computer processing generated. The tax is to be calculated using
the applicable method outlined in the bill, depending upon whether the AI
computer processing subject to tax was performed by a controlled processor or a
contracted processor.

If the AI computer processing
is performed by a contracted processor, the value generated by AI computer
processing equals the number of tokens required to perform the AI computer
processing, multiplied by the billing rate per token charged by the AI computer
processor. If the AI computer processing is performed by a controlled
processor, the value generated by AI computer processing is to be calculated
pursuant to a method of calculation approved by the Division of Taxation
(division) for the respective AI computer processor.

When AI computer processing is
performed by an AI computer processor located outside the State for a qualified
AI business, the amount of tax otherwise imposed is to be apportioned on the
basis of the percentage of the value generated by AI computer processing for
the qualified AI business that is attributable to AI system services used for
or intended for business uses within the State.



Records of Taxable AI Computer
Processing

The bill requires an AI
computer processor and a qualified AI business each to retain records of AI computer
processing, in such form and manner as the division may require, and to submit
the records to the division at such intervals as the division requires or upon
request.

An AI computer processor's records
are to include, but not be limited to: (1) the scope and nature of AI computer
processing performed, including information verifying the AI system services
for which the AI computer processing was used, and the qualified AI business
for which the AI computer processing was performed; (2) the total volume of AI
computer processing performed by the AI computer processor in its capacity as a
controlled processor and in its capacity as a contracted processor,
respectively; (3) the total value generated by AI computer processing,
performed by the AI computer processing in its capacity as a controlled
processor and in its capacity as a contracted processor, respectively,
including the method of calculation; (4) the amount of AI computer processing
performed in this State and the value generated by AI computer processing for a
qualified AI business that is attributable to AI system services used for or
intended for business uses within the State; and (5) any other information the
division requires.

A qualified AI business's
records are to include, but not be limited to: (1) the scope and nature of AI
computer processing consumed, including information verifying the AI system
services for which the AI computer processing was used, and the AI computer
processor that performed the AI computer processing; (2) the total volume of AI
computer processing used by the qualified AI business, including the total
volume performed by a controlled processor and a contracted processor,
respectively; (3) the total value generated by AI computer processing used by
the qualified AI business, including, but not limited to, receipts documenting
the consideration paid to any contracted processor for the performance of AI
computer processing; (4) the value generated by AI computer processing used by the
qualified AI business that is attributable to AI system services used for or
intended for business uses within the State; and (5) any other information
required by the division.



AI Workforce Impact Transition
Fund

The bill dedicates revenues
from the tax to the "AI Workforce Impact Transition Fund," to be established in
the Department of Labor and Workforce Development (department) under the bill. 
The monies in the fund are dedicated for: (1) training services in support of
displaced workers transitioning to an alternate career, including, but not
limited to, the selection of an alternate career; and the provision of, or
assistance in accessing, career training; (2) grants to qualified organization
for the design, planning, and implementation of training programs and services
in support of displaced workers; and (3) funding student support services and
dual enrollment programs in public high schools. The department is required to
publish information online about the support available, including how an
individual may access that support. The bill defines a "displaced worker" as
an individual whose employment is terminated or whose job is expected to become
obsolete within 12 months due to the current or expected operation of an AI
system or the performance of AI system services therefor.

The bill restricts related administrative
costs to 10 percent in any fiscal year but allows an exception for certain
start-up expenses. The bill requires the State Employment and Training
Commissioner (SETC) to design criteria and conduct an annual evaluation of the training
services provided through the AI Workforce Impact Training Fund. The
commissioner is required to publish an annual report to the Governor and the Legislature
within six months of the conclusion of each fiscal year that includes: the
total revenues deposited into the fund from each source; the total amounts
expended from the fund for each authorized purpose; grants provided, including
the amount and, if applicable, the names of recipient organizations; the number
of workers supported; the total number of workers who have become reemployed;
administrative spending; relevant State Employment and Training Commission
evaluation data; and any other information which the commissioner determines is
pertinent to the evaluation of the training services provided through the AI
Workforce Impact Transition Fund.
